To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Auditory training improves neural synchrony in human auditory brainstem.

1) the neural encoding of the syllable /d/ by the human auditory brainstem is improved by auditory training in children with a learning impairment, 2) this change is evident as an improvement in the precision of neural encoding, 3) this change is observed in the neural response to the syllable in noise, 4) the change in neural encoding is correlated with changes in cortical physiology as well as with changes in auditory, cognitive, and academic measures of performance.
auditory training improves neural timing, as measured by the brainstem response, in the human auditory system.

the plasticity of the brain's auditory system and the role of the brainstem in auditory processing.
the plasticity of auditory neural timing, and how it can be improved through auditory training.

this study provides the first direct evidence that auditory training can alter preconscious brainstem encoding of acoustic stimuli in children with language-based learning problems, and that this change is correlated with changes in cortical physiology and behavior.

auditory training improves neural synchrony and neural encoding of the speech sound structure in children with learning problems, and that the improvement is related to changes in the brainstem and cortex.
auditory training can alter preconscious neural encoding and that these changes in neural processing can be related to perceptual, academic and cognitive improvements.

the auditory training program improved neural timing in the brainstem, as well as cortical physiology, and this was related to improved speech perception and cognitive function.

auditory brainstem responses can be used to measure the efficacy of auditory training in individuals with learning impairments.
